finding.summary: Design doc's `HostAdapter` snippet is stale after this PR changed the interface
finding.evidence: The doc (updated elsewhere in this same PR) still declares `draft(items: readonly DebugItem[]): Promise<DraftResult>` and `send(bundle: Bundle): Promise<SendResult>` in the *The `HostAdapter` seam* section. `packages/debug-report/src/host.ts` now declares `draft(...): Promise<unknown>` (deliberately raw, per its own docblock) and `send(bundle, captures: readonly CapturePayload[])`. `HostAdapter` is the seam the whole SP1→SP2 substitution argument rests on, so the canonical doc showing two wrong signatures is exactly the drift design-doc discipline exists to prevent — and the doc was touched in this PR, so it was in scope.

verdict.reason: Both claimed mismatches are real and verified. docs/design/debug-report.md:314-315 declares `draft(items: readonly DebugItem[]): Promise<DraftResult>` and `send(bundle: Bundle): Promise<SendResult>`, while packages/debug-report/src/host.ts:82-83 declares `draft(items: readonly DebugItem[]): Promise<unknown>` and `send(bundle: Bundle, captures: readonly CapturePayload[]): Promise<SendResult>`. The drift is not benign simplification: host.ts:72-81 explicitly argues that declaring the validated `DraftResult` shape at this seam "would have been a lie every implementation told" and that "a second host honouring the declaration would produce a payload the parser silently drops every draft from" — i.e. the doc documents precisely the signature the code deliberately rejected. Likewise the `captures` second parameter and its `CapturePayload` rationale (host.ts:38-45, split out so the bundle stays small enough for localStorage) appear nowhere in the doc; a grep for CapturePayload/captures in the doc returns only unrelated prose (lines 66, 160, 263). This is in the design-doc-discipline lane and blocking as `major`: docs/design/debug-report.md is the canonical, README-linked doc (docs/design/README.md:162), host.ts:23 points implementers back to it as the design of record, and the doc's central SP1→SP2 "substitution rather than a rewrite" argument (lines 322-324, 489, 521) rests on this exact seam. No guard, no alternate doc with correct signatures, and no "illustrative/elided" marker on the snippet, so no refutation ground applies.

Nothing ignores that path: the root `.gitignore` ignores `.harness-reports/`, `.hunt/`, `.worktrees/` etc. but not `.wb-reports/`, and no other `.gitignore` in the tree mentions it. searchedFor: Grep 'wb-reports' across the repo (15 files, none a .gitignore)
Read of root .gitignore in full (195 lines)

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `report-endpoint.ts:63` sets `REPORT_DIR = ".wb-reports"` and lines 257-265 mkdir/writeFileSync decoded capture images plus `bundle.json` under `<repoRoot>/.wb-reports/<sessionId>/`; `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:200` supplies `repoRoot: path.resolve(__dirname, "../..")`, the actual repository root. I enumerated every `.gitignore` in the tree (Glob `**/.gitignore` returns exactly 4: root, backend, frontend, sheets) and grepped all of them for `wb`, `report`, and leading-dot directory patterns — the root file's artifact entries are `.harness-reports/` (173), `.worktrees/` (180), `.superpowers/` (189), `.pnpm-store/` (192), `.hunt/` (194), and nothing matches `.wb-reports/`; there is no `.wb-*`, `*reports/`, or `.*/` catch-all. I also ruled out the non-obvious ignore channels a counterexample could live in: `.git/info/exclude` holds only the default commented template, a repo-wide grep finds no committed `core.excludesFile` redirection, no script appends the entry (whole-repo grep for `wb-reports` hits only source/docs/tests), the plugin does not write a self-ignoring `.gitignore` into the created directory, and `packages/debug-report/` ships no `.gitignore` of its own. Blocking under this lens: the design doc (docs/design/debug-report.md:319-321) and task list (docs/tasks/active/20260821-debug-report-todo.md:141-143) make the on-disk `.wb-reports/<session>/` drop the handover mechanism, and the repo's own convention for such generated report dirs is an ignore entry (docs/tasks/archive/2026/02/20260228-harness-report-artifacts-todo.md:19 records exactly that step for `.harness-reports/`; design-editor docs repeatedly lean on "gitignored, so leftovers are invisible to git status"). The feature as landed therefore leaves its required artifact directory tracked, contrary to the established pattern it explicitly follows.

finding.summary: The plugin re-declares the core item/target data model instead of type-importing `../types`
finding.evidence: `draft-endpoint.ts` defines its own loose `Rect`, `Target`, `Item` and `DraftBundle` types that shadow `Target`, `DebugItem`, `Environment` and `Bundle` in `packages/debug-report/src/types.ts` — the same package, one directory up. The file's stated reason for not statically importing the core (Node cannot resolve extensionless relative imports from `vite.config.ts`) applies to VALUES; `import type` is fully erased and would not affect Node resolution, which is why `DRAFT_SCHEMA` (a value) needs `ssrLoadModule` but the shapes do not. `report-endpoint.ts` likewise re-declares a narrowed `BundleParse`. Two copies of the item model in one package is exactly the drift the doc's "one schema, no second copy" reasoning rejects for the schema.

verdict.reason: The duplication is present exactly as described. draft-endpoint.ts:47-79 declares local `Rect`, `Target`, `Item` and exported `DraftBundle` that mirror the canonical `Target` (types.ts:34-72), `DomElementRef` (types.ts:81-86), `DebugItem` (types.ts:145-160), `Environment` (types.ts:169-178) and `Bundle` (types.ts:180-188) in the same package; report-endpoint.ts:37-40 re-declares a narrowed `BundleParse` shadowing `ParseResult` (types.ts:190-192). The file's own stated reason for not importing the core (report-endpoint.ts:47-57, draft-endpoint.ts:132-139) is a VALUE-resolution constraint — which is why `parseBundle`/`DRAFT_SCHEMA` go through `ssrLoadModule` (report-endpoint.ts:58-60) — and does not apply to erased type-only imports; the same directory already imports with explicit `.ts` extensions for Node resolvability (plugin/index.ts:10-17, report-endpoint.ts:35), and sibling modules type-import these very shapes (ui/appearance.ts:9, ui/handover.test.ts:2). No guard exists: grep shows `DraftBundle` only inside draft-endpoint.ts, so nothing tests conformance with the canonical model, and renderItem/renderPrompt (draft-endpoint.ts:82-130) would silently emit `undefined` after a rename or a new target kind. Duplication/reuse is in this lens's lane and the repo explicitly treats a second copy as the fault (docs/design/cli.md:1711-1714, docs/design/harness-engineering.md:3133-3136) — the same "one schema, no second copy to drift" reasoning the plugin docblock invokes. The only mitigating reading (loose types intentionally model unvalidated input, cast at report-endpoint.ts:290) argues for deriving from the canonical types rather than re-declaring them, so it does not refute the finding.
